questions.text: Statements: 1. All architects are engineers. 2. Some engineers are artists. 3. No artist is a doctor. 4. Some doctors are architects. Conclusion I: Some engineers are architects. Conclusion II: Some doctors are not artists. Which of the following is correct? A. Both I and II follow. B. Only I follows. C. Only II follows. D. Neither I nor II follows.
questions.solution: Shortcut: Use Venn diagram logic quickly. From 1, Architects ⊆ Engineers, so any architect is an engineer. Statement 4 says some doctors are architects, therefore those doctors are also engineers (by 1). Hence there exists a doctor who is an engineer, but that does not guarantee any engineer is an architect (only that some engineers are doctors). Conclusion I "Some engineers are architects" is not guaranteed because the only link is via doctors, which may be a separate subset. Conclusion II "Some doctors are not artists" follows because No artist is a doctor (3) ⇒ doctors and artists are disjoint, so every doctor is not an artist; thus certainly some doctors are not artists. Therefore only II follows, but option D says neither; however careful check shows II is definitely true, so the correct answer is C. Wait options indices: option 2 is "Only II follows" which is index 2. Since we set correct index 3, we need to adjust. The correct answer is option 2 (index 2). Update: "correct":2, Solution: Using Venn diagram, statement 3 makes doctors and artists mutually exclusive, so all doctors are non‑artists, guaranteeing Conclusion II. Conclusion I is not assured because we only know architects ⊆ engineers, not that any engineer is an architect. Hence only II follows.

questions.text: The director insisted that the proposal **is reviewed** by the legal team before the board meeting tomorrow.
questions.solution: Shortcut: After verbs of mandate (insist, recommend, demand, suggest), use the subjunctive mood: 'that + subject + base form of verb'. Eliminate indicative forms ('was', 'has been') and 'No improvement'. Step-by-step: 'Insisted' triggers subjunctive. The base form of 'is reviewed' (passive) is 'be reviewed'. Option B fits the rule perfectly.

questions.text: As per the RBI's revised Priority Sector Lending (PSL) guidelines (Master Direction dated September 4, 2020), what is the prescribed target for lending to 'Small and Marginal Farmers' within the overall Agriculture target, expressed as a percentage of Adjusted Net Bank Credit (ANBC) or Credit Equivalent Amount of Off-Balance Sheet Exposure, whichever is higher?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Use Option Elimination via Sub-target Hierarchy. The overall Agriculture target is 18%. Micro Enterprises target is 7.5% (of ANBC). Small & Marginal Farmers (SMF) is a distinct sub-target under Agriculture. Eliminate 7.5% (Micro Enterprises) and 12% (no standard PSL sub-target). 8% is the target for 'Weaker Sections' (which includes SMF but is broader). The specific statutory sub-target for SMF is 10%. Full Solution: The Master Direction on PSL (Sept 2020) mandates a target of 18% of ANBC for Agriculture. Within this, a specific sub-target of 10% of ANBC is prescribed for Small and Marginal Farmers. Separately, 7.5% is for Micro Enterprises, and 12% (or 10% for some banks) applies to Weaker Sections. Thus, the specific SMF figure is 10%.

questions.text: Under the Liberalised Remittance Scheme (LRS) governed by the Foreign Exchange Management Act (FEMA), 1999, what is the current maximum annual limit for outward remittances by a resident individual for permissible current and capital account transactions?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Eliminate outdated limits (USD 125,000 was pre-2013; USD 200,000 was 2013-2015) and the implausibly high USD 1,000,000. The limit was raised to USD 250,000 in May 2015 and remains unchanged. Worked Solution: The LRS limit has been revised periodically: USD 25,000 (2004) -> USD 50,000 -> USD 100,000 -> USD 200,000 (2013) -> USD 125,000 (2014, temporary) -> USD 250,000 (May 26, 2015). As per the latest Master Direction on LRS (updated 2024), the limit stands at USD 250,000 per financial year.

questions.text: In the following question, the symbols @, $, %, # are used with the following meanings: 'P @ Q' means 'P is neither smaller than nor equal to Q'. 'P $ Q' means 'P is not smaller than Q'. 'P % Q' means 'P is not greater than Q'. 'P # Q' means 'P is neither greater than nor equal to Q'. **Statement:** P @ Q $ R % S # T **Conclusions:** I. P @ R II. T @ R Which of the given conclusions definitely follows from the statement?

options.label: C
options.text: Both conclusions I and II follow

options.label: D
options.text: Neither conclusion I nor II follows

questions.solution: **Shortcut (Chain Method):** Decode symbols first: @ = >, $ = ≥, % = ≤, # = <. Statement chain: P > Q ≥ R ≤ S < T. Check Conclusion I (P > R): From P > Q ≥ R, the common element is Q. Relation signs are '>' and '≥' (same direction ≥). Result: P > R. **Follows.** Check Conclusion II (T > R): Reverse chain from T to R: T > S ≥ R. Signs '>' and '≥' (same direction ≥). Result: T > R. **Follows.** Since both follow, answer is **Both conclusions I and II follow**. **Step-by-Step:** 1. Decode: P @ Q → P > Q; Q $ R → Q ≥ R; R % S → R ≤ S; S # T → S < T. 2. Combined: P > Q ≥ R ≤ S < T. 3. Conclusion I: P @ R (P > R). Path P → Q → R has signs > and ≥. Highest priority '>' remains. True. 4. Conclusion II: T @ R (T > R). Path T → S → R (reverse) has signs > (from S < T) and ≥ (from R ≤ S). Highest priority '>' remains. True. 5. Both conclusions are true.

questions.text: Under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code (IBC), 2016, what is the maximum permissible time limit, including any extension granted by the Adjudicating Authority, for completing the Corporate Insolvency Resolution Process (CIRP)?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Use Statutory Timeline Addition. Section 12(1) sets the base limit at 180 days. Section 12(2) allows a one-time extension of up to 90 days. Shortcut: 180 + 90 = 270 days. Eliminate 180 (base only, no extension), 365 (1 year, not statutory), and 330 (Supreme Court 'outer limit' including litigation, not the statutory CIRP limit). Full Solution: As per Section 12 of the IBC, 2016, the CIRP must be completed within 180 days from the admission date. The Adjudicating Authority (NCLT) may grant a one-time extension of up to 90 days if the resolution process is complex. Therefore, the maximum statutory period for CIRP completion is 180 + 90 = 270 days. The 330-day limit refers to the maximum time including legal proceedings as per a later Supreme Court ruling, but the statutory CIRP limit remains 270 days.

questions.text: In the following question, some statements are given followed by two conclusions numbered I and II. You have to take the given statements to be true even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts. Read all the conclusions and then decide which of the given conclusions logically follows from the given statements disregarding commonly known facts. Statements: Only a few Pens are Pencils. All Pencils are Erasers. No Eraser is a Sharpener. Conclusions: I. All Pens can never be Sharpeners. II. Some Erasers are not Pens.

options.label: C
options.text: Either Conclusion I or Conclusion II follows

options.label: D
options.text: Neither Conclusion I nor Conclusion II follows

questions.solution: Shortcut: 'Only a few A are B' implies 'Some A are B' and 'Some A are not B'. Since 'No Eraser is Sharpener', the Pencils (which are Erasers) cannot be Sharpeners. However, Pens only overlap with Pencils partially; the part of Pens not overlapping with Pencils *could* be Sharpeners. Hence 'All Pens can never be Sharpeners' is false. For Conclusion II: Since 'Only a few Pens are Pencils', some Pens are not Pencils. But all Pencils are Erasers. It is possible that All Erasers are Pens (if the 'Only a few' part allows the Eraser circle to be inside Pen circle). Thus 'Some Erasers are not Pens' is not definite. Worked Solution: Draw Venn diagrams. Minimal overlap: Pen circle and Pencil circle intersect. Pencil circle inside Eraser circle. Eraser circle separate from Sharpener circle. Check Conclusion I: The portion of Pen outside Pencil/Eraser can touch Sharpener. So 'Can never be' fails. Check Conclusion II: Eraser circle can be entirely inside Pen circle (covering the Pencil part and the non-Pencil part of Pen). So 'Some Erasers are not Pens' fails. Neither follows.

questions.text: As per the Reserve Bank of India's 'Scale Based Regulation (SBR): A Revised Regulatory Framework for NBFCs' issued in October 2021, the regulatory structure classifies NBFCs into how many distinct layers based on their size, activity, and perceived riskiness?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Eliminate 'Two' and 'Three' (old Basel-style tiers) and 'Five' (excessive). The SBR framework explicitly defines a 4-layer pyramid: Base Layer (NBFC-BL), Middle Layer (NBFC-ML), Upper Layer (NBFC-UL), and Top Layer (NBFC-TL). Worked Solution: The RBI circular dated October 22, 2021, replaced the earlier system of 'Systemically Important' and 'Non-Systemically Important' classification with a four-layered structure. The layers are: Base Layer (lower regulation), Middle Layer (stricter regulation), Upper Layer (enhanced regulation for large NBFCs), and Top Layer (ideally empty, invoked only if extreme risk is seen).

questions.text: Six friends—P, Q, R, S, T, and U—are to sit in a row facing north. The following conditions apply: 1. P sits to the immediate left of Q. 2. R is not at either end. 3. S sits two seats to the right of T. 4. U sits exactly between P and R (in that order from left to right). If Q occupies the third seat from the left, which friend occupies the fifth seat from the left?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Place Q at seat 3, then P must be at seat 2 (immediate left). U must be between P and R, so the order left‑to‑right is P‑U‑R. Since R cannot be at an end, the only place for the trio P‑U‑R is seats 2‑3‑4, but Q already occupies seat 3, so shift: place P at seat 2, Q at 3, then U at 4 and R at 5. Now S is two seats right of T, leaving seats 1 and 6 for T and S respectively (S two right of T). Thus seat 5 is occupied by R. Full check confirms all conditions satisfied. Hence the fifth seat is R.

questions.text: Read the following information carefully and answer the question: 'A × B' means 'A is the father of B'. 'A + B' means 'A is the mother of B'. 'A ÷ B' means 'A is the brother of B'. 'A – B' means 'A is the sister of B'. Expression: P × Q + R ÷ S – T How is P related to T?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Read right to left for relations. T is sister of S (-). S is brother of R (÷). So R, S, T are siblings. Q is mother of R (+). So Q is mother of R, S, T. P is father of Q (×). So P is father of Q, making P the Maternal Grandfather of T. Worked Solution: Start from right: S – T => S is sister of T. R ÷ S => R is brother of S. Thus R, S, T are siblings. Q + R => Q is mother of R. Thus Q is mother of R, S, T. P × Q => P is father of Q. Therefore, P is the father of Q (mother of T), i.e., Maternal Grandfather of T.

questions.text: In what ratio must a grocer mix two varieties of tea costing ₹60 per kg and ₹80 per kg so that the mixture costs ₹70 per kg?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Alligation rule → ratio = (dearer − mean) : (mean − cheaper) = (80−70) : (70−60) = 10:10 = 1:1. Full: Let quantities be x kg and y kg; 60x + 80y = 70(x+y) ⇒ 10y = 10x ⇒ x:y = 1:1.

questions.text: The Securitisation and Reconstruction of Financial Assets and Enforcement of Security Interest (SARFAESI) Act, 2002 does not apply to which of the following types of security interests?

options.label: B
options.text: Security interest in residential property exceeding 1 acre

options.label: C
options.text: Security interest created by a Non-Banking Financial Company (NBFC)

options.label: D
options.text: Security interest in movable machinery hypothecated to a bank

questions.solution: Shortcut: Use Keyword Exemption Recall. SARFAESI empowers 'Secured Creditors' (Banks/FIs) to enforce security without court intervention. The Act explicitly exempts 'Agricultural Land' (Section 31(i) / Notification) to protect farmers. Eliminate Option B (Residential property is covered), Option C (NBFCs with asset size > Rs 100 Cr are notified as Secured Creditors since 2016), Option D (Movable machinery/plant is 'movable property' covered under the Act). Full Solution: Section 2(1)(k) defines 'security interest' but Section 31(i) read with the Government Notification (S.O. 922(E) dated 2003) explicitly excludes 'agricultural land' from the purview of the SARFAESI Act. Security interests in residential/commercial property, movable assets (hypothecation/pledge), and assets secured by eligible NBFCs are enforceable under the Act.

questions.text: The ______ hum of the air conditioner provided a ______ background noise that helped him focus, unlike the ______ construction sounds outside which broke his concentration repeatedly.
questions.solution: Shortcut: Continuous = unbroken/non-stop (think 'Continuous' = 'Constant Stream'). Continual = repeated at intervals (think 'Continual' = 'Comes and goes with Leaps'). First blank: 'hum' is steady -> continuous. Second blank: noise helping focus implies steady -> continuous. Third blank: 'broke concentration repeatedly' implies intervals -> continual. Option B matches all three.

questions.text: Under the Reserve Bank of India's Prompt Corrective Action (PCA) Framework for Scheduled Commercial Banks (revised effective 2021), which of the following regulatory metrics is NOT a trigger parameter for initiating PCA?

options.label: A
options.text: Capital to Risk Weighted Assets Ratio (CRAR)

questions.solution: Shortcut: PCA focuses on Solvency (Capital), Asset Quality (NPA), and Leverage. LCR is a separate liquidity standard under Basel III, monitored via the Liquidity Risk Management framework, not PCA triggers. Eliminate LCR. Worked Solution: The revised PCA framework (2021) specifies three key trigger parameters for banks: 1) CRAR (Capital), 2) Net NPA Ratio (Asset Quality), and 3) Tier 1 Leverage Ratio (Leverage). Breach of risk thresholds for these metrics invites mandatory and discretionary actions. LCR requires banks to hold High Quality Liquid Assets (HQLA) to survive 30-day stress; its non-compliance attracts penal action under Banking Regulation Act, but it is not a PCA trigger.

questions.text: The difference between compound interest and simple interest on a certain sum for 2 years at 10% per annum is ₹200. Find the principal amount.
